paragraphs.source_en: A similar composition competition took place in 1818. Taking part in it, Keats wrote to his brothers, "The Wednesday before last [February 4] Shelley, Hunt, and I, wrote each a sonnet on the river Nile." paragraphs.source_en: It was not just English poets who sought to evoke the Sahara. Johann Wolfgang von Goethe published West-östlicher Diwan, or West-East Divan, in 1819 and an updated version in 1827. Diwan is a twelve-book collection of lyrical poetry and Goethe's last major poetic cycle. A lifelong admirer of Middle Eastern cultures, Goethe saw in the East the pre-classical roots of western civilization, including the origins of language and poetry, and his magnum opus as both an exchange of cultural ideas between Occident and Orient and a philosophical or spiritual journey.
